▸ 0. Boot the stack (postgres · redis · gateway · jaeger · worker · dashboard)
▸ 1. Register a demo agent version: deny-by-default allowlist + approval gate + hard budget

▸ 2. Create a run under that deny-by-default budget
▸ 3. Drive the policy engine (POST /v1/runs/{id}/check-tool) — the governance proof
▸ 4. Immutable audit trail — every decision was appended (no UPDATE/DELETE path exists)
▸ 5. Run state + the budget the platform is enforcing
(budget auto-kill fires on step submission over the cap — see Part B / submit_step_result)
▸ 6. OTel / GenAI spans — every enforce decision is one
(decision spans still flushing — open Jaeger and filter tag ferrumdeck.decision=deny)
▸ 7. Golden-trace replay (deterministic metric wire-contract regression — pure, no stack)
(skipped — needs uv/Python; the governed API checks above are the Docker-only core)
▸ 8. Coherence-divergence live-fire (deterministic — a drifting run is caught + R-tiered)
(skipped — needs uv/Python; deterministic dev extra, not part of the Docker-only core)
Live signal (Part B / real agentic run): a divergence writes an
audit_events row with violation_type=coherence_divergence, emits the SSE
event, and surfaces on the run's Coherence card. Set FERRUMDECK_COHERENCE_MODE=enforce
to gate an R3 divergence (run → WaitingApproval) instead of only recording it.
Optional full agentic loop (needs ANTHROPIC_API_KEY): ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-... make eval-run
why_frozen: A measurement must not depend on the git history of whoever runs it. Re-harvesting changes the corpus and therefore the published rate, so it is a deliberate act (`--reharvest`) that forces a re-measure, not a side effect of running the eval on a different checkout.
